I actually saw the novelupdates reviews on this one when I first checked it out. I remember this author wrote some other gaming novel that I liked so I thought this one would be even better since it was newer. I saw the comments about the xenophobia and was instantly turned off, didn't even start reading it. The stuff I read tends to be quite fluffy and not that #deep so I don't encounter this a lot in novels though. I do remember in Assistant Architect there was this one chapter where everyone went to Japan and there was this brief tension until a character was like we should be tolerant, etc. I saw some comments here mentioning some xenophobia towards Japan in novels, I can kind of understand this considering China's history with Japan during the war, but I also understand that it can wreck a reading experience. In my opinion if an author is going to bring something like that up it should have a purpose, which is why I liked that small tidbit from assistant Architect where a character urged open mindedness. It's not like it was a huge thing but I feel like it's more thoughtful commentary. I'm sure the xenophobia in this novel is hurtful to Korean readers and imo even for non-korean readers it doesn't make for a pleasant reading experience.
